gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured power figure for the UGREEN NASync DXP2800: OCinside measured about 7 W at idle and a 34.7 W peak under a combined CPU, RAM and disk stress test with two 4 TB WD Red Plus drives in RAID 1.
standout_why: Compared against Starry Hope's best-NAS-for-Plex page (cites KitGuru ~24 W idle for the DXP4800 Plus and Notebookcheck 37–42 W for the DXP6800 Pro, both over $500, plus Lon.TV's N100 mini-PC transcode test, but nothing measured on any under-$500 NAS), Terabytewise (no measured figures at all, no named reviewer), and NAS Decoded (states it does no lab testing; no watts, dB or stream counts). None gives a named measurement for the DXP2800, F2-425 Plus, F4-425, F2-423 or AS5402T. Caveat: Starry Hope's separate DXP2800 model page (not in ChatGPT's results) does relay the OCinside figure, so it is new to the cited set rather than new to the web. No named reviewer's measured count of simultaneous 4K HEVC hardware transcodes on any candidate NAS could be found, so the angle cannot decide the pick.
decides: Confirms rather than changes the pick: the DXP2800 idles near 7 W (roughly 61 kWh a year if left on), so the N100 2-bay is cheap to run as an always-on Plex box. For the F2-425 Plus and AS5402T only maker power/noise specs exist, not independent measurements, so the page should label them as such. Because no named lab has published a measured 4K-HEVC stream count for any candidate, the page should say that plainly instead of printing estimate tables like ChatGPT's '2–4 streams' row.

findings.label: Idle power, measured
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 review – Practical testing (OCinside)
findings.note: OCinside: 'In idle mode, the NAS only requires approx. 7 watts.' Test unit fitted with two WD40EFPX 4 TB WD Red Plus drives in RAID 1 (Btrfs) plus NVMe SSDs listed on page 1 of the review; price note on page 1 dates testing to 12/2024. No author byline shown.

findings.label: Peak power, measured
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 review – Practical testing (OCinside)
findings.note: OCinside: 'We measured a maximum power consumption of 34.7 watts' under a combined CPU, RAM and hard-disk stress test. Same drive setup as the idle figure.

findings.label: RAID 1 write throughput, measured
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 review – Practical testing (OCinside)
findings.note: 50 GB file written to the two-drive RAID 1 Btrfs volume in 290 s. iperf3 averaged 950 Mbit/s but on a 1 GbE test network, so it does not show the 2.5GbE port's limit.

findings.label: Noise under drive access (relayed)
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 – Starry Hope model page
findings.note: Starry Hope attributes 34.2 dB to ComputerBase with two IronWolf Pro 20 TB HDDs in access. Secondhand: the ComputerBase page itself was not opened, so treat as unverified until it is. UGREEN's own quiet-mode rating is 29–34 dB (maker spec).

findings.label: Power, maker spec (not independently measured)
findings.source_title: TerraMaster F2-425 Plus – Starry Hope model page
findings.note: TerraMaster spec with two Seagate 4 TB drives, N150 model. Noise spec 20 dB with two drives in standby at 1 m in a 17.3 dB(A) room. ITPro (Dave Mitchell, 23 Feb 2026) and Fstoppers (Zhen Siang Yang) both describe the fan as very quiet but publish no dB figure.

findings.label: 5GbE SMB throughput, measured
findings.source_title: TerraMaster F2-425 Plus review: A versatile desktop NAS at a great price (ITPro)
findings.note: Dave Mitchell, ITPro, 23 Feb 2026, Iometer over 5GbE against a mirrored pool of two Kingston NVMe SSDs; iSCSI over dual-5GbE MPIO 7 Gb/s read / 5.1 Gb/s write. Figures confirmed via Starry Hope's summary; the ITPro page itself loaded only to the design section. CNX Software measured iperf3 at 4.71 Gb/s over 5GbE on a TerraMaster-supplied unit (https://www.cnx-software.com/2026/03/28/terramaster-f2-425-plus-nas-review-part-2-configuration-benchmarks-and-ai-enhanced-media-storage/). Not a transcoding measure.

findings.label: Power and noise, maker spec (not independently measured)
findings.value: 22.9 W operation / 12.7 W disk hibernation / 0.71 W sleep; 18.6 dB HDD idle
findings.note: Spec table reproduced by NASCompares (Eddie Webguy, 25 Jul 2023). Drive configuration and measuring distance not stated. No Plex stream test on the page.

findings.label: Intel N100 concurrent Plex transcodes (relayed, mini PC not NAS)
findings.source_title: The Best NAS for Plex in 2026 Has an Intel Chip With Quick Sync (Starry Hope)
findings.note: Starry Hope (Jim Mendenhall, updated 2 Nov 2026) quotes Lon.TV's test of an Intel N100 mini PC: a 4K VP9 file and a Blu-ray MKV transcoded 'without significant CPU load', and five concurrent transcodes reached about 35% CPU. Mixed sources, not all 4K HEVC, and not run on a NAS; Lon.TV's own page not opened.

unsourced: A named reviewer's or lab's measured count of simultaneous 4K HEVC-to-1080p hardware transcodes (with bitrate and HDR tone-mapping state) on any candidate NAS: UGREEN DXP2800, TerraMaster F2-425 Plus, F4-425, F2-423 or Asustor AS5402T. Searched NASCompares, Neowin, Android Central, ITPro, Fstoppers, CNX Software, Igor's Lab, Notebookcheck; none publishes one.
